observations: The page number «( 18 )» stands at the head of the page, centred. The page has no footnotes and no signature.

L01-L13: the places of the fractions: the first place is that of the degrees, «graduum», where the whole number stands, the second that of the minutes, the third of the seconds, the fourth of the thirds, and so on to the ninth and tenth place. A whole number by a whole number gives a whole number, a whole number by a fraction a fraction of the same kind: two degrees by two minutes, four minutes; three degrees by six thirds, eighteen thirds. Minutes by minutes give seconds; the products of seconds by seconds, thirds by thirds and fourths by fourths are printed as thirds, fourths and fourths (see the critical note). The rule: the places of the two factors are joined, and the number is found as for whole numbers.

L14-L24: six minutes by seven minutes, forty-two seconds, minutes being parts of sixty and their products parts of 3600; seven seconds by nine minutes, sixty-three thirds, which are one second and three thirds, seconds being parts of 3600 and their products with minutes parts of 216000, «ducentis milibus et xvi. milibus», which are thirds, 216000 being sixty times 3600.

L25-L34: one and a half multiplied «in duo et dimidio» (see the critical note): each factor made ninety minutes; ninety by ninety, «.viii. milia et .c.» seconds, 8100; divided by sixty, «.c.xxx.ta vque» minutes, 135; divided by sixty, two degrees and «xvi.» minutes, printed for fifteen (see the critical note), «que sunt quarta unius»: one and a half by one and a half is two and a quarter.

L30: the vertical bar between «queque» and «lx», with a word space on each side, marks the beginning of fol. 108 verso of the manuscript, which the note in the left margin, «car. 108 verso.», names; transcribed as a margin note.

Numerals: L14 «vii.», L16 and L17 «lx.» at the beginning of the line, L17 «ex lx. in lx.,», L19 «quoque lx.», L21 «ex lx.,», L23 «xvi.», L29 and L32 «per lx.,» and L34 «xvi.» without the opening point. Raised letters: L30 «lx» and «ii» with «ta» and «da», sixty seconds, the raised letters set above the numerals, «ta» over the x and «da» over the two i; L31 «.c.xxx.ta vque», one hundred and thirty-five, and L32 «.lx.ta», with the raised letters after the numerals.

L01 «rentie: prima» (12 px) and L08 «.iiii. minuta» (11 px, median 15.5 px) have a space. The pencil underline of «quare» shortens the measured gap after the colon of L20 «tercia :»; the gap to «quare» is 20 px.

critical_notes.printed: secunda in secundis tercia; et tercia in terciis quarta ; et quarta in quartis quarta
critical_notes.proposed: secunda in secundis quarta; et tercia in terciis sexta; et quarta in quartis octaua
critical_notes.evidence: the rule that follows (L11-L12), «coniunctis utrasque differentias quas multiplicas inuicem», joins the places of the two factors, and the cases the page works follow it: degrees by minutes give minutes and degrees by thirds thirds (L07-L09), minutes by minutes seconds (L09-L10, L14-L15), seconds by minutes thirds (L18-L20); by it seconds by seconds give fourths, thirds by thirds sixths and fourths by fourths eighths, where the print has thirds, fourths and fourths. The fault may lie instead in the second factors: seconds, thirds and fourths by minutes give thirds, fourths and fifths
critical_notes.impact: the three products are wrong as printed; the rule and the worked examples are right

critical_notes.evidence: the working is that of one and a half by one and a half: the first factor is made ninety minutes, and «Iterum fac unum et dimidium quem uis multiplicare in eadem minuta, et erunt similiter .xc.» (L26-L28) makes the second, also one and a half, ninety minutes; ninety by ninety, 8100 seconds, 135 minutes, two degrees and a quarter (L28-L34). Two and a half would be 150 minutes, and ninety by 150 gives 13500 seconds, 225 minutes, three degrees and three quarters
critical_notes.impact: the example names a second factor that its working does not use; the working and the result are right for one and a half by one and a half

critical_notes.evidence: 135 minutes (L31) divided by sixty give two degrees and fifteen minutes, and the text calls the minutes «quarta unius», a quarter of one, which is fifteen minutes
critical_notes.impact: the result reads two degrees and sixteen minutes for two degrees and fifteen
